cards.name: Run speed ramp and stick shaping
cards.summary: Walk and run speed use linear ramps of a fixed number of updates, and the stick is shaped by a 0.1 dead zone rescaled over 0.9.
cards.behavior: The helper that raises speed adds a fixed step each update and stops at the cap. If speed is already above the cap it returns the speed unchanged, so a boost is never clipped by it. The braking helper removes a fixed step equal to the speed cap divided by the brake frame count, and it clamps at zero without crossing to the other sign. A second brake form clamps at a floor instead of zero. Stick shaping removes a dead zone of 0.1 and rescales the rest to the 0 to 1 range, keeping the sign. Default tuning gives a run cap of 14, a minimum run speed of 3, a 40 update ramp up and a 10 update brake. A separate speed threshold of 14.5 marks a dash. The ground move controller that applies these ramps is a header only, so the exact per update step is unverified. Treat the numbers as tuning targets. The values are defaults and a parameter file can replace them.

cards.name: Jump power scaled by run speed
cards.summary: Jump power blends linearly between a minimum and a maximum by forward speed, with a gravity of 1.5 and a fall speed cap of 35.
cards.behavior: A helper maps forward speed to jump power. It clamps speed between a low and a high bound, turns the position into a 0 to 1 factor, and blends from the minimum jump power to the maximum. If the two powers are equal it returns the maximum at once. Default jump powers are 17 and 19.5, so a standing jump is only slightly lower than a full run jump. Rising and falling both use a gravity of 1.5 per update, and falling speed is capped at 35. The jump keeps 70 percent of ground speed as air inertia. A hold-to-extend window of 10 updates exists in the tuning table. The air move controller that applies the hold extension, forward acceleration and turning is a header only, so how held input changes the arc is unverified. The speed bounds passed to the blend come from callers that are not in this repository.

cards.name: Jump buffer, triple jump chain and quick-turn window
cards.summary: A jump press is remembered for 5 updates, three chained jumps must land within a 10 update window, and a quick turn arms a 20 update window for the turn jump.
cards.behavior: Jump buffer: each update the remaining count drops by one down to zero, and a fresh press sets it to 5. The judge says yes if the button was pressed this update or the count is above zero, and always says no while a forced slope slide is active. Chain: a counter wraps at 3 each time a jump starts and a timer restarts at zero. While the counter is above zero the timer grows each update and at 10 the chain clears. If the caller reports that counting must stop, the chain clears at once, which is how landing late or touching down ends it. The second and third jumps use higher powers and lower or equal gravity: 21 with gravity 1.5, then 25 with gravity 1.0. Quick turn: when the quick-turn trigger fires the counter is set to 20, then falls by one each update; the turn jump is allowed while the trigger is on or the counter is above zero. The turn jump itself and the squat jump are not decompiled here, only their tuning: both launch at power 32 with gravity 1.0.

cards.name: Long jump from the crouch slide
cards.summary: A long jump is allowed while sliding in a crouch and moving forward, launches at speed 14 with a low gravity of 0.48, and can reach speed 23.
cards.behavior: The crouch brake state allows a long jump only while it is in its brake phase and the velocity points along the facing direction. On the first update a helper sets the launch velocity from the tuning values: initial speed 14, a vertical push of 12, a forward move power of 4 and a minimum speed of 2.5, with the jump inertia rate of 0.7. The helper bodies are not in this repository, so the exact blend is unverified. Each later update calls a shared diving-jump mover with forward accel 0.25, brake 0.5, speed cap 23, speed floor 2.5, side accel 0.25 and gravity 0.48, plus the fall cap of 35 and an orientation slerp of 0.4. A ceiling hit reflects the vertical speed, and the state ends on ground contact. A chain counter wraps at 3 and resets after 15 updates without a new long jump; it only picks which animation plays.

cards.name: Ground pound
cards.summary: The ground pound pauses in the air, then drops at speed 45 with gravity 45, and its landing allows a jump cancel from update 5 to 30.
cards.behavior: Start requires the button press and at least 40 units of height above the ground. The Start phase zeroes velocity and plays a wind-up, then moves to Fall when the animation ends. On the first Fall update the velocity is pushed along gravity by 45, and every Fall update pushes by 45 again, each with a limit argument of 45, so the fall is very fast. The helper that applies the limit has no body here, so whether the limit clips total speed or only the push is unverified. A ground contact while the button is held starts an 8 update cooldown on further impact messages and records the contact point. When the player reaches walkable ground the state moves to Land. On the first Land update a knock-down message is sent to what was hit, and the landing counts as weak when the ground moved less than 10 units along gravity since the contact. Landing offers a jump cancel only on update 5 through 30 and free movement from update 24. The tuning table also holds a stronger enemy bounce of 35 for after a pound, with no decompiled consumer.

cards.name: Head-first dive
cards.summary: The dive converts motion to a horizontal burst of 20 plus an upward kick of 28, with no forward acceleration afterward and a heavy gravity of 2.0.
cards.behavior: On the first update the velocity splits into a horizontal part and a vertical part. The horizontal direction is kept, or the facing direction is used when the player is standing still. If the player was falling, the vertical part is cleared. A fixed upward kick of 28 is then added and the horizontal speed is set to 20. Later updates call the shared diving-jump mover with forward accel 0, brake 0.5, speed cap 20, floor 2.5, side accel 0.125 and gravity 2.0. So the dive cannot gain speed, only steer slightly and brake, and it falls fast. The state flags a water-entry animation when a deep-water dive is possible and ends on ground contact. The mover body is not in this repository; the arguments are what the state passes.

cards.name: Wall slide and wall jump
cards.summary: A wall contact in the air starts a slide, a buffered jump press turns it into a wall jump of speed 8.6 and power 23, and input is locked for 25 updates.
cards.behavior: The wall state starts in a Slide sub-state. While sliding, a buffered jump press records the jump on the wall history and switches to Jump. The slide ends if the wall judge fails, and the leave is recorded with the wall normal. In Jump the first update sets horizontal velocity to 8.6 along the facing direction, reversed unless the toward-wall flag is set, and faces the player that way. It then configures the air mover with an air speed cap of 100, an initial speed of 8.6, a vertical power of 23, gravity 0.95 and a 25 update input lock. The argument meaning follows the order used by another caller; the mover body is absent. A ceiling hit reflects vertical speed. The state ends on ground contact. The wall judge can pull the player back to Slide during the jump if a wall is found again. The slide gravity of 0.5 is in the tuning table, but the slide state body is a header only.

cards.name: Wall stick conditions
cards.summary: A wall sticks only when falling, facing within 60 degrees of the wall, at least 120 units above ground, and a 77 unit probe from 120 units up hits the wall.
cards.behavior: The judge runs each update and clears first. It fails for a 2D model, a forced run, fewer than 10 updates since an upper punch, a ground below 120 units, ground contact, no wall contact, walls flagged as no-stick, and a carry state that forbids sticking. A wall history check also rejects repeated sticking to the same wall. The velocity must be non-zero and pointing downward. The facing direction must be within 60 degrees of the wall normal. A stick push that leans slightly away from the wall, between 0 and the cosine of 60 degrees against the wall normal, rejects the stick. The vertical speed must not be near zero. A probe 77 units long starts 120 units above the feet and aims into the wall, and it must hit. If the contact is on a wall face the judge passes. Otherwise it probes 50 units to each side of a point 5 units inside the wall, and each side normal must be within 20 degrees horizontally and 30 degrees vertically of the main wall normal unless a collision border exists.

cards.name: Ledge catch judge
cards.summary: A ledge catch uses a 43 degree ledge angle, an edge-top height of 120 and a bottom height of 150, and fails while carrying, in a forced run or on the ground.
cards.behavior: The judge fails while carrying, in 2D, in a forced run, under an external force, when not touching a wall, on the ground, or when the wall forbids grabbing. The facing line is the facing direction, or the stick direction when a deep stick push trigger is on. The wall contact point is shifted by the moving platform velocity. A search helper then looks for a catchable edge using the stick cone of 60 degrees, a ledge angle of 43 degrees, an edge-top height of 120, a bottom height of 150, a body radius of 55 and a standing radius of 45. The search helper is not decompiled, so the geometry test is unverified. Tuning for the climb itself (speed 70, a climb angle of 40, and jump-from-ledge speeds 20 up and 3 forward) has no decompiled consumer.

cards.name: Ceiling grab judge
cards.summary: Grabbing a ceiling requires a tagged surface, no carry and no external force, and a search within 100 units using a 50 unit body radius.
cards.behavior: The judge fails when carrying, in 2D, under an external force, or when the touched surface carries no grab code. Three surface kinds are handled: a wall, a ceiling and a ground face. For a wall, the player must not be moving away from it unless a snap force exists, and the contact point is moved by the platform velocity before a wall-hit search runs. For a ceiling or ground face the same velocity check applies and a no-wall search runs. Both searches use the player height of 160, a reach of 100 and a body radius of 50. When a ceiling is found, a hang axis is chosen: the stored axis is flipped to match the velocity if the player moves faster than the minimum run speed, otherwise to match the facing direction. The searches are not decompiled, so the geometry is unverified. Swing and ceiling jump tuning (jump power 20, move 15 and energy thresholds 6.5 and 10) has no decompiled consumer.

cards.name: Slope slide
cards.summary: Sliding accelerates along the downhill direction by 0.3 per update up to speed 22, with weak steering of 0.6 side accel, and keeps at least speed 5 on entry.
cards.behavior: The slide starts when the pound button is held and a ground test passes. The ground test is not decompiled, so the start angle of 26 degrees and end angle of 10 are tuning values whose use is inferred from their names. On entry the velocity along the downhill direction is raised to at least 5, then clamped to the speed cap of 22. Each update the controller splits velocity into a downhill part and a side part. If the player moves uphill the downhill part is multiplied by the brake 0.9. Downhill acceleration is the accel of 0.3 times an angle factor and a speed factor, then limited to the cap. The side part is multiplied by 0.98 and the stick adds side speed at 0.6 per update up to 10. A forced-slide surface changes the numbers: uphill motion is zeroed instead of braked by 0.9, side accel 0.2, side brake 0.96, side cap 3 and a turn limit of 15 degrees instead of 5. The body is stuck to the ground by subtracting the ground snap force of 7 along the normal. The state ends after a landing that follows 30 or more updates in the air, or when, on ground gentler than the end angle, the slide has run 30 updates and speed is at or below 3.

cards.name: Roll trigger and slope roll tuning
cards.summary: A roll starts from a run at speed 14.5 or more while holding crouch, and the slope roll tuning allows speed up to 35 with a boost of 30.
cards.behavior: The direct-roll judge runs each update. It passes only on the ground, not carrying, not in a forced run, not in 2D, with crouch held, and with horizontal speed at or above the dash threshold of 14.5. A second judge decides roll starts from a trigger input on ground that is not a forced-slide surface. The roll state itself is not decompiled, so the following values are tuning only: start jump power 12, start speed 20, boost speed 30, max speed 35, accel 0.6, brake 0.998 per update, side accel 0.4, side cap 10, a restart interval of 15 updates, a restart charge time of 40 and a minimum roll length of 45 updates. The slope controller has a rolling mode that lets the player steer the slide with side input at the slide end. That mode is live code in the slope controller.

cards.name: Crouch slide and crouch walk
cards.summary: Crouching while running keeps 1.2 times the speed as a slide that brakes by 0.95 per update until speed 3.5, then a crouch walk moves at speed 3.5.
cards.behavior: On entering the crouch the backward part of the velocity is removed, unless the floor is a skate surface. If the player moves forward and the horizontal speed is at or below the run cap of 14, the speed is multiplied by 1.2, and it is set to zero if the result is not above the stop speed of 3.5. Faster speeds are left as they are. Each update an inertia slide multiplies speed by 0.95 (0.985 on skate floor) and allows slight side steering. The slide ends and the state waits when slide speed is at or below 3.5. A long jump is allowed during this brake phase. In the waiting and walking phases, a crouch walk sets horizontal velocity to 3.5 times the input direction, turns toward the stick, and holds the body down with the ground snap force. A stand-up judge gates leaving the crouch.

cards.name: Standing spin
cards.summary: The standing spin lasts 90 updates, brakes by 0.95 per update, and lets the stick add 0.5 per update up to the larger of the current speed and 8.
cards.behavior: On entry the spin direction follows the input. Each update the horizontal velocity is multiplied by 0.95, the speed cap is set to the larger of the current speed and 8, the stick direction adds 0.5, and the length is clamped to that cap. The ground snap force of 7 is then subtracted along the normal. The body faces the movement direction, or keeps its facing if the player is still. The state ends when the update count reaches 90. Spin jump tuning (power 20, gravity 0.4, move cap 8) and cap-spin frame counts also exist in the tuning table, but no decompiled state consumes the spin jump values.

cards.name: Cap throw timing and structure
cards.summary: Only the throw timing is verified: 12 updates for a ground spin throw, 8 in the air, 7 for a swing, 2 for a repeat, and a 10 update throw buffer.
cards.behavior: The cap actor is declared in a header with no bodies, so throw flight is not available. What can be read is the design. The header lists throw types: a spiral, a tornado, a rolling throw, a stay-in-place throw and a separate-play throw, plus phases for start, flight, brake, append, return, rebound, blow and lock-on. A parameter reader names the actor parameters that tune a throw, translated: throw height, top speed, repeat throw speed, brake time, reach distance, end point stop time, return strength and speed, turn limit angle, underwater versions of speed, reach and brake, tornado reach and reflect time, and rolling speed, reach and brake time. Their numeric values come from actor data that is not in this repository. The tuning table gives the spin-throw frame counts, a throw press buffer of 10 updates, and a repeat throw run of 20 updates with run speed 16 and a 60 update accel ramp.

cards.name: Cap catch window and cap-jump limits
cards.summary: A catch opens a 10 update window for follow-up actions, and the air cap jump is re-armed only by landing, with a height limit blocking climbs.
cards.behavior: Catch window: a counter grows each update and resets to zero on the catch trigger, and the catch counts as active while the trigger is on or the counter is at most 10. Re-arm: the land reset clears the height limit and re-arms the cap jump. A reset that only requires standing ground clears the limit but re-arms the jump only if the ground is flatter than the stand angle of 60 degrees. A wall-air reset clears only the height limit. Height limit: recording a limit stores the current position when the player is off the ground. The player is over the limit when airborne and above the stored point along gravity, which stops repeated cap jumps from climbing. The code here only re-arms the flag; the place that spends it is the cap actor, which is not decompiled. Tuning for the bounce-off-cap jumps: power 32 and gravity 1.0 from the ground, 26 in the air, a catch jump of 22 with gravity 1.3, and a small catch pop of 10.

cards.name: Capture transition
cards.summary: A capture plays a 15 to 30 update arc into the target with a stand-in that scales between 0.02 and 1, and the player may cancel after 13 updates.
cards.behavior: When a capture starts, the transition length is the sensor distance minus 200, divided by 30, rounded, plus 15, then clamped between 15 and 30 updates. The player body is hidden after the first update. A stand-in model grows from a scale of 0.02 to full size over the first 5 updates, then shrinks back to 0.02 over the last 4 updates before the end of the transition. The stand-in follows a path from the start to the target, lifted along a sine arc by up to 400 units against gravity. The player position is interpolated linearly toward the captured actor over the whole length. At the end the player copies the pose and velocity of the captured actor every update, so control passes to that actor. A cancel is allowed only after 13 updates in the hold phase and only when no hack sensor is still starting. Ending the capture restores the model and plays a short jump animation.

cards.name: Captured flap flight
cards.summary: Each flap sets a vertical speed of 15 (23 on a swing flap), the climb is capped 230 above the highest point reached, and gravity is 0.6 when falling.
cards.behavior: A flap press, or a motion swing, sets the vertical speed, the sideways accel and the animation rate. Default flaps use vertical speed 15, accel 1.0 and animation rate 1.6. Swing flaps use 23, 1.5 and a rate of 2.3. The only decompiled user overrides two header defaults, the swing animation rate (2.6 to 2.3) and the turn angle (20 to 15), so those are the effective values. The state remembers the highest point reached. While below it, every update holds vertical speed at the flap value, adds 4 along gravity, and scales horizontal speed by 0.95 and vertical by 0.7. At or above it, the vertical speed eases by a factor of 0.1 toward a target that rises up to 230 over the old best across 30 updates, and above that band the state pulls the height back toward the band and zeroes vertical speed. If no flap comes within 21 updates the state drops to Fall. Fall adds gravity 0.6 and scales horizontal speed by 0.95 and vertical by 0.94 each update. A flap while falling zeroes vertical speed and enters a hover of 20 updates with no gravity, and another flap during or after the hover resumes rising. Ceiling and wall contact cancel the speed into the surface, scaled by 1.1. A bounce off an enemy adds an upward speed of 20.

cards.name: Damage knockback and invulnerability
cards.summary: A hit pushes back at speed 2, hops at 12 with gravity 0.95, then grants 240 updates of invulnerability with the body flickering every 6 updates.
cards.behavior: On a hit in 3D the player is thrown backward by a push of 2 along the facing direction. The air mover is set up with an air cap equal to the jump air cap, the push, a hop of 12, gravity 0.95 and an input lock of 9999 updates, by argument position. A different trigger, whose meaning the source does not name, keeps the horizontal speed, faces against it and sets the hop from the vertical speed. In the air the state watches for walkable ground, then lands, brakes along the ground normal, plays a land animation and can be cancelled 45 updates into the landing. After 120 updates in the air it ends. Invulnerability: a damage call sets the counter to the value its caller passes (the tuning default is 240) and each update counts it down by one. The body is hidden when the counter divided by 6 has remainder zero, a flicker of 1 hidden update in 6. A star power timer of 1800 updates blocks damage, and a sound cue plays at 40 updates left. A kids mode heals one point after 600 updates, or 60 once the player has stood still for 120 updates.

cards.name: Underwater oxygen meter
cards.summary: Oxygen holds for 60 updates, then drains over 1380 updates, refills in 30, and deals damage every 300 updates once empty.
cards.behavior: The meter is a 0 to 1 value. While underwater a counter runs. After the no-drain delay of 60 updates the meter falls by 1 divided by the drain length each update and stops at zero. Once it is at zero a second counter runs and a damage event fires whenever that counter is a multiple of the damage interval. Surfacing refills by 1 divided by the refill length each update, to a maximum of 1, and zeroes both counters. The numbers are set by a setup call from a caller that is not decompiled, so the defaults from the tuning table are the best available. An ice-water variant has the same damage interval of 300 and a recovery of 70 updates.

cards.name: Deep-water dive and long-fall judges
cards.summary: A water-entry dive animation needs a drop of at least 1500 units to the water surface, and a long fall counts after 3000 units of falling.
cards.behavior: The dive judge fails if the fall distance is under 10 or if ground lies within 1500 units below. It then searches for a water surface along a line of length (height + 1500) divided by 2 below the player. The surface must be at least 1500 units below, and any ground under the player must be deeper than the water surface plus the player height, so a dive is chosen only over deep water. The action plays the dive animation unless the model is 2D, a carry is active, or the animation already plays. The long-fall judge is true when the tracked fall distance reaches 3000, and is false while dead, in 2D, bound, or captured. Swim speed, surface bobbing and dive tuning also exist, with consumers outside this repository: surface speed 9, spin boost speed 13, dive start speed 26.5.

cards.name: Ground snap force and gravity
cards.summary: On the ground the player is pulled into the surface by 7 per update along the normal, while free fall uses gravity 1.5 and the table gravity is 3.
cards.behavior: Ground states do not rely on free fall. They finish each update by subtracting the ground snap force of 7 along the ground normal from the velocity, so the body hugs slopes and stairs. The crouch walk, standing spin, slope slide and landing all use the same value. In the air the gravity is 1.5 per update with a fall cap of 35, and jumps override it with their own gravity. A general gravity of 3 appears in the tuning table and is passed to the crouch and landing helpers. The tuning table holds a small step height of 25, a body radius of 55 and a body height of 160; their consumers are collision code that is not decompiled. These are the defaults; a parameter file can replace each of them.

cards.name: Screen shake table
cards.summary: Eleven named shakes set a length in updates, a wave count and a strength, and a decaying cosine moves the projection offset.
cards.behavior: Each shake has a length in updates, a number of oscillations and a strength. A one-shot shake runs for its length. Each update the phase is the oscillation count times 360 degrees divided by the length, times the update count, and the offset is the cosine of the phase times the strength times the remaining fraction of the length, so it fades to zero. Both axes get the same offset, except the vertical type which zeroes the horizontal part. The offset feeds the projection, not the camera position. Starting a shake is ignored if the active shake outranks it; the comparison body is not shown. A caller can pass a length override and the oscillation count is scaled by the same ratio. A looping shake uses the cosine of the update count divided by 7.5 times two pi, with a strength of 0.0007 and no length. Table rows are listed as length, waves, strength: faintest 15, 2.5, 0.0015; weak 25, 2.5, 0.0025; medium 25, 2.5, 0.004; strong 30, 3.0, 0.008; strongest 45, 3.5, 0.015; extreme 45, 3.5, 0.05.

cards.name: Camera ticket switch and blend
cards.summary: The active camera is a ticket that hands pose data to the next one, blends over a set step count, and resumes with a 60 update blend after a stop.
cards.behavior: Camera behaviors are poser objects held by tickets. Each update the updater checks the switcher. If a new ticket was chosen, the updater collects facts from the old poser into a start record: its name and priority, whether to keep its distance, its swing angles and the look direction toward the next pose. It then starts the new poser and begins an interpolation of the step count the switcher gave. If no ticket remains the updater goes inactive. When the camera is stopped and later released, it starts a 60 update interpolation. A poser can also keep a local blend of 30 updates that starts when its target changes: it blends the previous camera and look-at positions to the new ones with a Hermite ease of slope 1.5, and the step counter then ends. Each poser update runs in this order: rotation input, gyro, the poser update, look-at easing, vertical absorption, snapshot controls, local blend, and the collision arrow. A look-at bounds box clamps the look-at point on each axis in the camera frame, rotated about the vertical axis, and shifts the camera by the same amount.

cards.name: Camera stick and gyro sensitivity
cards.summary: Camera rotation reads the stick with optional axis flips and scales it by a level table, and gyro input has three scales of 0.625, 1 and 1.6.
cards.behavior: The rotation stick is read from the camera input holder, with the horizontal or vertical axis negated when its reverse flag is set. A level from the scene parameter holder picks a scale. Stick levels -2 to 2 map to 0.44, 0.72, 1.6, 1.27 and 1.55, and any other level gives 1.0. The table is not monotonic in the decompilation, so a port should confirm the level order against a build before copying it. The scale is passed to the angle controller and the swing controller each update. Gyro levels -1, 0 and 1 map to 0.625, 1.0 and 1.6. A reset press resets the rotation, unless in snapshot mode. Target helpers give the horizontal speed, the vertical speed, the jump speed and the fall speed along gravity, which pollers use to decide framing.
